biography.plain_text: Christopher “Kit” Kernon was a British shipping executive and naval-architecture graduate who led Vitol International Shipping. After managing chartering across Asia and Australia, he spent more than two decades directing projects and time charters, later consolidating Vitol's shipping businesses in Singapore. He also served on Latvian Shipping Company's management and supervisory boards.

long_biography.plain_text:
Vitol's maritime operation depended on chartered tonnage, tanker expertise and the coordination of projects across energy markets. Kernon brought naval-architecture training from Newcastle University to that work. His early assignments covered Asia and Australia, followed by responsibility for global time-charter projects and six years on the management board of Latvian Shipping Company.

When Vitol brought its shipping subsidiaries together in Singapore, Kernon became chief executive of the consolidated business. The role extended a career that had already moved from technical study to commercial shipping leadership. He steered the operation as fuels and emissions expectations changed, including greater attention to LNG and lower-carbon transport. Vitol later described the division as a market leader under his stewardship. Kernon died on 6 November 2025, aged 56.
